summary: This is a truncated clipped NatureTTL web article titled "The Majestic Wildlife of Canada's Boreal Forest" by Donna Feledichuk. Its visible introduction describes her small town in Northern Alberta, where she sees whitetail deer, a red fox with kits, fourteen moose during the rut, and great grey owls raising owlets. The note ends before the article body, so the rest of the piece is not covered.
one_line: Donna Feledichuk describes the abundant wildlife around her small Northern Alberta town in this NatureTTL boreal forest article (truncated).
key_facts: The article "The Majestic Wildlife of Canada's Boreal Forest" was written by Donna Feledichuk and published on the NatureTTL website.
Donna Feledichuk lives in a small town in Northern Alberta, Canada.
The closest city to Donna Feledichuk's town is over two hours away.
Donna Feledichuk says she wakes up feeling blessed each day.
Whitetail deer eat from the bird feeders outside Donna Feledichuk's door.
A red fox is scurrying its kits to a new den near Donna Feledichuk's home.
Fourteen moose were seen within a kilometre of each other during the rut.
A mating pair of great grey owls returns each spring to raise a new set of owlets.
The article is filed under NatureTTL's Inspiration section, in the Wildlife category.
The visible text of the note ends during the introduction, before the main article body.
